body:
Minutes:

- Agenda and Meeting Management: Johnny Stenback addressed the meeting agenda, noting that previous attempts to remove agenda-plus items might have been too aggressive and encouraged participants to re-add items if necessary. They also requested that the group skip items that had already been discussed in previous meetings.
- HTML Canvas and Input Method Editor Privacy: For issue 10650 Olli Pettay raised concerns regarding the privacy implications of using Input Method Editor styling within HTML Canvas content editable elements, as this can leak information about the user's specific input method. Dan Clark suggested that exposing the color in the edit context might mitigate the fingerprinting risk associated with this issue.
- HTML Video Poster Image: Scott Jehl and Alexandra Moscowitz from Squarespace provided an update on issue 10378 regarding the HTML video poster image. They have submitted a pull request against the specification and have requested standard positions from vendors. As they are currently awaiting further feedback, it was decided that the agenda-plus label would be removed from the issue.
- Popover Light Dismiss: Keith Cirkel discussed an oversight in the popover light dismiss specification regarding the missing "command" and "select" items. While browsers currently implement this behavior, the specification needs to be updated. Tests have been authored for the Web Platform Tests, and the group is coordinating with Luke to ensure the pull request is finalized.
- Mutation Observer and Shadow Trees: Lea Verou presented issue 1287, which proposes a Mutation Observer flag to observe shadow root attachment to facilitate polyfilling HTML syntax. Anne van Kesteren expressed reservations about prioritizing polyfill support as a standardization goal, citing concerns about long-term maintenance. Lea Verou explained that this feature would assist with web component libraries and lazy loading. Olli Pettay and other participants noted the complexity of designing an API for this purpose, suggesting that the group should aim for a comprehensive design that handles shadow tree observation generally rather than adding fragmented, ad-hoc features .
- Light Dismiss UI Events: Joey Arhar discussed issue 11586, which involves changing light dismiss to use click events instead of pointer down and pointer up events. They expressed a desire to move forward with shipping this in Chromium to address user bugs, regardless of pending changes to the user interface events specification. Olli Pettay and Mason Freed discussed the status of the relevant specification, and Joey Arhar will continue to monitor the progress.
- Range Requests Security: Jake Archibald presented issue 1936, detailing how non-Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) range requests reveal file size information to cross-origin resources, a behavior currently observed in Chrome and Safari . Several options were considered, including storing range headers in a hidden way, providing dummy values, or forcing Cross-Origin Resource Sharing for these requests. Simon Pieters suggested that requiring Cross-Origin Resource Sharing for service workers is the safest approach, despite potential breaking changes. Jake Archibald will summarize the discussion on the issue, and Mason Freed agreed to help identify the appropriate point of contact at Chrome for further input.
- Reference Target Update: Dan Clark provided an update on the reference target proposal, specifically detailing the implementation of event redispatching using the related target mechanism. The speaker has updated the specification pull requests and implemented the changes in Chromium. Olli Pettay requested additional testing for complex, multi-level shadow DOM scenarios, and Dan Clark agreed to review the test coverage and address any gaps .
- Stages Document Update: Anne van Kesteren announced that the stages document has been updated to address community feedback and is available for final review.
- Scheduling and Closing: Johnny Stenback confirmed that there will be no meeting next week due to the Independence Day holiday in the United States. The group will reconvene in three weeks to continue the current schedule, as the following week falls on a conflicting time slot.
